neighbours.label: head word of an appositive phrase after a comma (X, a measure of ...; X, cheap metals)
fire: The patients took metformin, a drug that lowers blood sugar, twice a day.
We visited Lisbon, the capital of Portugal, in early spring.
Researchers measured cortisol, a hormone released under stress, in each sample.
The engineers chose aluminium and magnesium, light metals, for the frame.
Her grandfather, a retired sailor, still tells stories about the war.
The team studied the Amazon, the largest rainforest on Earth, for a decade.
Farmers added lime, a cheap mineral, to reduce the acidity of the soil.
They tracked heart rate variability, a marker of recovery, after each run.
quiet: The patients took metformin twice a day because it lowers blood sugar.
We visited Lisbon in early spring and loved its old streets.
Researchers measured cortisol in each sample because stress releases it.
The engineers chose aluminium and magnesium for the frame because they are light.
Her grandfather still tells stories about the war he fought as a sailor.
The team studied the Amazon rainforest for a decade with local guides.
Farmers added lime to the soil to reduce its acidity at low cost.
They tracked heart rate variability after each run to judge recovery.
